parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, entry rule, facility rule or documented police targeting appears; documented positives include a police-escorted Pride, broadcasting rules barring anti-LGBT incitement, and ministry health outreach to same-sex couples. Against that: same-sex conduct remains criminal and expressly reaches a visitor in a locally same-sex-classed relationship; official and religious hostility is on record; there is no discrimination law, no registerable advocacy body, and closed civic space, so recourse is thin. Healthcare friction is documented (2019 LGBTQ survey: 59% disrespected, 30% denied) though dated and not trans-specific. The 2015 killings are individual, dated incidents with no rate or homicide baseline. Border treatment of mismatched documents is unresolved. Adult-with-partner exposure is materially higher than adult alone; custody rules for accompanying minors are undocumented.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific entry, visa or screening rule is sourced. Whether border officials question documents that do not match presentation, and how a no-LGR passport is read, is explicitly unresolved.
entry_documents.protection: No documented border friction, marker-mismatch practice or document-examination rule against trans visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: An unresolved document question can convert into a criminal-law question, since same-sex conduct is criminal and relationships are unrecognised.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Common-law sodomy offences criminalise same-sex conduct for men and women as of 12 March 2026, and the dossier states a visitor in a locally same-sex-classed relationship falls under it. Courts sit under an absolute monarchy that upheld a morality-based registration refusal.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No arrest, prosecution or detention of a trans visitor is documented; no trans-specific offence exists; no police targeting of gender-nonconforming people is recorded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Outing at any stage (documents, lodging, a companion) can move an encounter from social friction into criminal exposure; enforcement frequency is undocumented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No bathroom, ward, custody-placement or strip-search rule for visitors appears anywhere in the record.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The only subnational content is two individual 2015-era killings in one town, which the dossier warns are incidents, not a regional pattern; no other town-level divergence is sourced.

care_services.exposure: 2019 survey: 59% of LGBTQ respondents disrespected or discriminated against at public health facilities, 30% denied services; source notes limited gender-affirming care. Dated and LGBTQ-wide, not trans-specific.
care_services.protection: 2013 National SRH Policy §4.3 requires services regardless of sex, gender, sexual orientation; 2012 ministry HIV outreach to same-sex couples; 2021 adolescent guidelines name LGBT people a key population.
care_services.interaction: Ministry-level policy sits beneath frontline practice, while the visitor has no registerable advocacy body to complain to.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Ministers and officials publicly condemned same-sex conduct (2012, 2017, 2021 report); pastors called it 'demonic'; the registrar refused LGBTI group registration on morality grounds in 2019 and again after the 2023 ruling.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2017 and 2022 broadcasting guidelines bar content inciting hatred on sexual-orientation grounds; 2021 guidelines define GBV to include gender identity; Supreme Court voided a registration refusal in June 2023.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing lowers the practical value of the paper protections, since the same administration still refuses registration.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. Adoption and relationship-recognition rules are resident-facing and do not reach a visiting guardian.
minors_guardians.interaction: No custody, detention-placement or family-classification rule for an adult travelling with a minor is sourced; outcome for that pairing is an open question, not an exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Two dated killings (a lesbian murdered March 2015, a gay man months earlier) in one town; documented significant societal stigma; no trans-specific killing rate and no general homicide baseline available, so magnitude cannot be stated.
street_violence_police_response.protection: July 2018 first Pride drew 2,000+ with police escort and was judged a success; 2021 virtual Pride held without incident; an LGBT-welcoming church reopened in 2018.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Acceptance signals are concentrated in the capital; whether they extend elsewhere is unevidenced expectation only.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No registered national advocacy body exists; LGBTI group registration refused (2019, upheld 2022, still refused 2023-26); no statutory anti-discrimination remedy; rated 'Not Free' 17/100 with closed civic space.
remedies_unknowns.protection: High Court accepted constitutional association, privacy and expression protections (2022); Supreme Court voided the registrar decision (2023); policy instruments name sexual orientation in equality and GBV frameworks.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Constitutional reasoning exists but no body can register to use it; border document treatment and post-2023 registration practice remain unresolved.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's Visitor Conduct Register, entry bar and airline verification are a documented universal-exposure mechanism hitting every trans visitor at every crossing. This dossier documents no such mechanism: no entry rule, no register, no screening practice. Its worst features are a latent same-sex-conduct statute plus tier-3 hostility, so it sits materially above 0.35-A.

Vesskar pairs a deception statute with routine bank/clinic/transport checks, documented detention, denial of care and scarce legal aid — universal daily exposure. Here there are no documented routine checks or detentions; exposure is hostility plus one criminal statute applied to relationships. Comparable thin-recourse weakness, but fewer recurring universal encounters, so slightly higher.

Marisol Union's ward-by-document rule creates a concrete universal facility exposure with only partial remedies. This dossier has no facility rule at all, but adds criminal liability for same-sex-classed relationships and a state that refuses to register any advocacy body. Similar partial-denial, weak-remedy profile; comparable level.

Vellmaris shows a documented stop resolved by national equality law, an accountability board apology and compensation. This jurisdiction has no equality statute, no registerable advocacy body and closed civic space, so equivalent friction would carry no working remedy — placing it clearly below 0.65-A.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a hostile-law, thin-recourse jurisdiction without a documented trans-specific enforcement machinery. The heaviest operative items are the criminal same-sex-conduct statute that expressly reaches a visitor in a locally same-sex-classed relationship (raising adult-with-partner risk well above adult-alone), official and religious threat-framing, and the total absence of any advocacy body or discrimination remedy inside closed civic space. Against this, no trans-specific offence, border rule, facility rule or police targeting is documented, and real acceptance signals exist: a police-escorted Pride, broadcast hate-speech rules, ministry health outreach, and a Supreme Court voiding a registration refusal. Dated 2015 killings and a 2019 LGBTQ-wide healthcare survey support, but do not measure, present risk. Undocumented border treatment of mismatched documents remains the key open question. Net: Elevated Risk.
